Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

putior 0.2.0

Breaking Changes

  • Renamed putior_skills() to putior_guide(). The function, its MCP tool (putior_guide), and its ACP operation (guide) all use the new name. putior_help("skills") still works as an alias for backward compatibility. The inst file was renamed from SKILLS.md to GUIDE.md, and the vignette from skills.Rmd to ai-integration.Rmd.

  • put(), put_auto(), put_generate(), and put_merge() now default to recursive = TRUE (previously FALSE). Directory scans now include subdirectories by default. Pass recursive = FALSE for the old behavior. (#34)

  • put_diagram() output now starts with a frontmatter block that keeps Mermaid 11’s drawing on Mermaid 12 renderers that set a theme: GitHub has drawn Mermaid 12’s “neo” look, with labels wrapped at 120px, since it moved to Mermaid 12.1.0 in October 2026. The block sets the dagre layout, the classic look, a 200px wrapping width and no minimum node width; it sets no theme, so the page’s light or dark theme still applies. Mermaid 9.3.0 to 11.17.2 draw the same with or without it. The new argument mermaid_config takes "classic" (the default), "none" for the previous output, or a named list written as the configuration. The title, if any, shares the frontmatter. The MCP put_diagram tool has the same argument. Mermaid reads the frontmatter only at the very start of the diagram code, and versions before 9.3.0 not at all: text in front of it, such as an %%{init}%% line, makes the diagram fail to parse, so use mermaid_config instead, or "none" for such hosts. (#54)

  • put_diagram() output now also carries accessibility metadata for screen readers, right after the flowchart line: accTitle with the title, if one is given, and accDescr with a summary such as “Workflow with 4 steps and 3 data files.” (.internal variables are not counted as files). Mermaid puts them into the SVG’s <title> and <desc>; the frontmatter title alone does not (Mermaid 10.5.0 and later). The title is escaped so that Mermaid shows it as written: like labels, plus < and %%{, which Mermaid’s sanitizer and directive handling would change. Mermaid reads these lines from 9.1.0 on; for an older renderer use accessibility = FALSE together with mermaid_config = "none". The MCP put_diagram tool has the same argument. ?put_diagram and GUIDE.md now list the Mermaid versions that putior supports and that its CI tests. A decision node with the id accDescr is now written as node_accDescr: accDescr{ started an accDescr block, and the node lost its shape and label. (#50)

  • With show_artifacts = TRUE, put_diagram() now draws each data hop once, through the file’s node (script --> file --> script). Before, it also drew a direct edge between the two scripts, so every hop appeared twice and the diagram had about 1.5 times the edges it needed, which brings Mermaid’s 500-edge limit closer. A script that another script reads (such as utils.R) has no file node and keeps its direct edge. artifact_edges = "both" draws the direct edges as before; the MCP put_diagram tool has the same argument. (#55)

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed show_source_info = TRUE using <small> HTML tags that are unsupported by GitHub’s Mermaid renderer. Source file names are now shown without HTML formatting tags. (#32)
  • Fixed pipe characters (|) in node labels breaking Mermaid diagram parsing. Pipes are now escaped using the #124; entity. (#33)
  • put() now gives annotations without an id a fallback id (node_1, node_2, …) when the uuid package is not installed. Before, such annotations had no id: if none had one, put_diagram() failed with a misleading “missing required column(s): id” error, and if only some had one, it silently dropped the others. This broke the quick-start example and the sandbox templates for anyone without uuid. The sandbox now also shows diagram errors in its status line instead of a blank preview. (#58)
  • Fixed logging, which wrote nothing with logger 0.3 or later: every log call failed inside logger and the error was hidden. The putior.log_level option, set by set_putior_log_level() or for one call by the log_level argument, is now the only threshold, and an invalid log_level is an error. With logger installed, WARN-level messages now appear on stderr next to the matching R warnings. (#70)
  • Fixed single-line block comment annotations (/* put ... */) silently losing their last property, which could drop an output and its edge. (#72)
  • put_merge() no longer merges a manual annotation and an auto-detected file into one node when their ids meet: auto-detected rows get a suffix when their id (also in its Mermaid form, where 1 is node_1) is already used, so an unannotated node_1.R next to an annotation with the fallback id node_1 stays separate. It also matches manual and auto-detected rows by file path, so an annotated x/load.R no longer hides an unannotated y/load.R, and with merge_strategy = "supplement" or "union" no longer takes the inputs and outputs detected in the other file. (#74)
  • Annotation values may now contain the other kind of quote: label:"Don't panic" and label:'Say "hi"' keep their labels. Before, put() dropped any value with a quote character in it, without a warning, and the node showed its id instead; the troubleshooting vignette even recommended label:"Load 'raw' data". There are still no escapes, so a value cannot contain its own kind of quote, and backslashes in Windows paths stay as they are. A property that put() cannot read is now named in its validation warning (with validate = TRUE, the default) instead of being dropped silently, and is_valid_put_annotation() returns FALSE for such a line. An annotation that ends with a continuation \ (without a comma before it) on the last line of the file no longer loses its last property. put_generate() wraps a value that contains a double quote in single quotes, so that put() reads its suggestions back unchanged. (#91)
  • A comment may now follow the values of an annotation, as the put() help page, the vignettes and the cheatsheet have always shown (# put id:"a", label:"Load" # first step). Before, the comment made the last property unreadable, and it was dropped. Outside quotes, whitespace followed by #, --, // or % after a value starts the comment. In a multiline annotation, a comment may also come before the continuation \ of a line. (#91)
  • put_diagram() gives every node one Mermaid id and uses it in the node definition, edges, class lines and click directives. Before, edges to an artifact whose path has two punctuation characters in a row (such as ./raw data (v2).csv) used a different id than the artifact node, so Mermaid drew an extra unlabeled node and left the artifact unconnected. Annotation ids that differ only in punctuation (a-b and a_b) were merged into one node with a self-loop; they now stay two nodes (a_b, a_b_2) and put_diagram() warns. Two data files whose names differ only in punctuation get two artifact nodes. put_auto() and put_generate(), which derive ids from file names, now give files that would share an id (a-b.R and a_b.R, end.R and node_end.R, or load.R in two folders) distinct ids (load, load_2). put_generate(output = "file") now writes each annotation next to the file it belongs to; when a file in between gave no annotation, the next one went into the wrong .put file. (#46)
  • Node ids that are Mermaid keywords (end, graph, flowchart, subgraph, style, class, classDef, click, linkStyle, call, href, interpolate, and the link targets _self, _blank, _parent, _top) made the whole diagram fail to parse. They are now written as node_end and so on. id:"end" is a natural name for a pipeline’s last step. (#45)
  • With source_info_style = "subgraph", subgraph ids are now file_<name> and never equal a node id. Before, a file load.R with a node id:"load" failed to render (“would create a cycle”) on Mermaid 11, and on Mermaid 12, which GitHub uses, the node silently disappeared. Files with the same name in different folders now get one subgraph each instead of sharing one, and the subgraph label then includes as much of the folder path as it takes to tell them apart (x/load.R, a/x/load.R). (#45, #46)
  • With show_files = TRUE, edge labels are now quoted and escaped like node labels (-->|"raw data (v2).csv"|). A file name with parentheses or other special characters made the diagram fail to parse. (#45)
  • The title of put_diagram() is now written as a quoted YAML string. A title with : (such as "ETL: stage 1") made the diagram fail to parse, and text after # was dropped as a YAML comment. (#45)
  • A # in a label that Mermaid would read as a character entity is now escaped as #35;. Mermaid decodes #<name>; and #<digits>;, so a label such as Step #35; was shown as Step #. A plain # (C#, item #1) is left alone. ?put_diagram now describes how labels and ids are written. (#45)
  • put_diagram() and the MCP and ACP servers accept direction = "TB", Mermaid’s synonym for "TD". GUIDE.md named TB as the default, but "TB" was rejected with an error. (#79)
  • Labels that contain Mermaid syntax are now written so that Mermaid shows them as written. Mermaid read a line with direction, whitespace and TB, BT, RL or LR (and TD from Mermaid 11.17.2 on), as in “Change direction LR to TB”, as a direction statement and dropped it: the node lost its label, and with source_info_style = "subgraph" a file named direction LR.R made the diagram fail to parse. That whitespace is now written as an entity (direction#32;LR). The same rule spans line breaks, so an edge to an id ending in direction (wind_direction) followed by an edge from an id starting with LR (LR_prep) lost both edges; such an edge now ends with ;. On a line where style or classDef comes before it, in the label or in the node id, a : followed by an escaped character, as in style:"bold" (written style:#quot;bold#quot;), is now written as #58;: Mermaid removed the last ; of such a line and showed style:"bold#quot. (#89)

New Features

MCP Server Integration

  • Added putior_mcp_server() to expose putior functions as MCP tools for AI assistants
  • Added putior_mcp_tools() to get/filter tool definitions for custom MCP integrations
  • 16 tools available: put, put_diagram, put_auto, put_generate, put_merge, get_comment_prefix, get_supported_extensions, list_supported_languages, get_detection_patterns, get_diagram_themes, putior_guide, putior_help, set_putior_log_level, is_valid_put_annotation, split_file_list, ext_to_language
  • Supports Claude Code, Claude Desktop, and other MCP-compatible clients
  • Tools return JSON (workflow data as one object per node) or plain text. They print nothing, because with the stdio transport stdout is the protocol channel, and never write files or the clipboard, so every tool except set_putior_log_level is read-only. The put_diagram tool scans a path and returns the Mermaid code. (#65)
  • The put_diagram tool takes a source argument: annotations (the default) scans with put(), auto draws the workflow that put_auto() detects, and merge combines both like put_merge(), with merge_strategy. When a scan finds nothing and R warned (the directory is empty, no file matches pattern, a file cannot be read), the scan tools now fail with R’s warnings instead of returning [] or empty text: the warnings never reached the client. When nothing warned, put_diagram says what is missing for its source: no annotations (and it suggests source = "auto"), or no file that put_auto() can analyze. (#73)

ACP Server Integration

  • Added putior_acp_server() to expose putior as an ACP agent for inter-agent communication via REST API
  • Added putior_acp_manifest() for agent discovery
  • Supports natural language requests for all core operations
  • Input path sanitization to prevent directory traversal attacks

Multi-Language Comment Syntax (30+ Languages)

  • Added support for 30+ programming languages with automatic comment prefix detection
  • Comment styles: # (R, Python, Shell, etc.), -- (SQL, Lua, Haskell), // (JavaScript, TypeScript, C/C++, Go, Rust, Java, etc.), % (MATLAB, LaTeX)
  • Added get_comment_prefix(), get_supported_extensions(), ext_to_language()
  • Added list_supported_languages() to enumerate all supported languages

Auto-Detection Patterns (18 Languages, 902 Patterns)

  • Full auto-detection for: R, Python, SQL, Shell, Julia, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java, C, C++, MATLAB, Ruby, Lua, WGSL, Dockerfile, Makefile
  • Pattern inheritance: TypeScript extends JavaScript, C++ extends C
  • Single authoritative language registry (R/language_registry.R)

LLM Detection Patterns

  • 54 patterns for modern AI/ML libraries across R and Python
  • R: ellmer, tidyllm, httr2 (API requests)
  • Python: ollama, openai, anthropic, langchain, transformers, litellm, vllm, google generative AI, groq

Auto-Annotation Feature

  • Added put_auto() for automatic workflow detection from code analysis
  • Added put_generate() for generating PUT annotation comments (roxygen2-style)
    • Now supports output = "raw" for programmatic access
  • Added put_merge() for combining manual and auto-detected annotations
    • Three merge strategies: “manual_priority”, “supplement”, “union”

Colorblind-Safe Themes

  • Added 4 viridis family themes for accessibility:
    • viridis: Purple-blue-green-yellow (general accessibility)
    • magma: Purple-red-yellow (high contrast, print-friendly)
    • plasma: Purple-pink-orange-yellow (presentations)
    • cividis: Blue-gray-yellow (deuteranopia/protanopia optimized)
  • All themes perceptually uniform and tested for color vision deficiencies

Custom Theme API

  • Added put_theme() for creating custom color palettes (#39)
  • New palette parameter on put_diagram() accepts putior_theme objects
  • Override individual node types (input, process, output, decision, artifact, start, end)
  • Base theme inheritance — customize only what you need. An override keeps every key it does not set from the base theme’s style for that node type, including the text color and the border width (3px for start and end nodes, 1px for artifacts); earlier development versions dropped the unset keys and forced a 2px border (#61). If an override changes how light fill is, set color too, so the label stays readable

Block Comment Annotations

  • Added PUT annotation support inside /* */ and /** */ block comments (#37)
  • Use * put as line prefix inside block bodies for all //-prefix languages
  • Supports single-line block comments and JSDoc-style patterns

File Exclusion

  • Added exclude parameter to put(), put_auto(), put_generate(), and put_merge() for regex-based file exclusion (#38)

WGSL Shader Language Support

  • Registered .wgsl with // comment prefix (#31)
  • 17 auto-detection patterns for GPU bindings, textures, samplers, and naga-oil imports

Dockerfile Support

  • Handle extensionless Dockerfile via .FILENAME_MAP (#35)
  • 13 detection patterns for FROM, COPY, ADD, EXPOSE, VOLUME, CMD, RUN

Makefile Support

  • Handle Makefile and GNUmakefile via .FILENAME_MAP (#36)
  • 10 detection patterns for include, wildcard, target rules, install, shell commands

Metadata Display

  • Added show_source_info parameter to put_diagram() for displaying source file information in diagram nodes
  • Added source_info_style parameter with “inline” and “subgraph” display options

Clickable Hyperlinks

  • Added enable_clicks parameter to put_diagram() for making nodes clickable
  • Added click_protocol parameter: “vscode”, “file”, “rstudio”
  • Click directives include line numbers when available

Structured Logging

  • Optional logger package integration for debugging annotation parsing
  • Log levels: DEBUG, INFO, WARN (default), ERROR
  • Added set_putior_log_level() for configuration
  • Per-call override via log_level parameter on core functions

S3 Workflow Class

  • Workflow data frames now have putior_workflow S3 class
  • Added print.putior_workflow() for concise workflow summaries
  • Added summary.putior_workflow() for structured summary information

Interactive Sandbox

  • New run_sandbox() opens an interactive Shiny app for trying PUT annotations: paste or type annotated code, simulate several files, and see the workflow diagram update as you edit (needs the shiny package)
  • Added copy-to-clipboard button for quick Mermaid code export
  • Added optional shinyAce syntax highlighting (graceful degradation)
  • The sandbox loads Mermaid 12.2.0 from jsdelivr, pinned with a Subresource Integrity hash (#48). It draws diagrams in Mermaid 11’s classic style (dagre layout, classic look, 200px label wrapping, no minimum node width), which putior’s themes are made for and which GitLab, Quarto and VS Code show. GitHub moved to Mermaid 12 in October 2026 and draws putior diagrams in the neo look with labels wrapped at 120px (#54). A diagram with a syntax error shows Mermaid’s error message. Mermaid 12 needs a current browser (ES2024; Safari 17.4 or later)
  • File markers (# ===== File: name.R =====) are read one line at a time, with any spaces or tabs around them, at least three = and an optional closing run, so an unclosed marker no longer takes the next file with it and a name containing = is recognized. When two simulated files have the same name (ignoring case), both are kept, the later one in a copy_2/ folder, and the status line says so; so does text before the first marker, which is ignored. File names are made safe to write on Windows (trailing dots dropped, characters such as : or ? replaced), and a file that still cannot be written is left out with a note instead of emptying the whole diagram (#53)
  • If Mermaid cannot be loaded from jsdelivr (no network, a blocked CDN), the preview says so instead of staying blank, and the copy button and the Mermaid Code tab still work. A diagram that changes while the preview is hidden is drawn as soon as the preview is visible again, whether its tab is shown or a collapsed pane is opened (#64)

Documentation

  • Documented all valid node_type values across vignettes and reference (#40)
  • 8 comprehensive vignettes including quick-start, annotation guide, features tour, API reference, showcase, troubleshooting, quick-reference, and AI integration
  • Professional cheat sheet (inst/cheatsheet/putior-cheatsheet.qmd)
  • 20 example files in inst/examples/
  • putior_guide() and putior_help() for in-session reference

New Helper Functions

  • resolve_label() internal helper to reduce code duplication in diagram generation
  • sanitize_acp_path() for ACP input validation
  • normalize_path_for_url() for cross-platform path handling
  • generate_click_url() for creating protocol-specific URLs
  • generate_click_directives() for Mermaid click action generation
  • generate_file_subgraphs() for file-based node grouping

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed ACP put_generate() called with invalid output = "raw" (now supported)
  • Fixed MCP theme enum missing viridis family themes
  • Fixed documentation using deprecated name instead of id in examples
  • Fixed ACP theme extraction regex missing colorblind-safe themes
  • Replaced unsafe 1:nrow() loops with seq_len(nrow()) to handle empty data frames
  • Moved %||% operator from acp.R to zzz.R for shared access

Improvements

  • put_diagram() warns when a diagram is over Mermaid’s default limits of 500 edges (maxEdges) or 50,000 characters (maxTextSize). Renderers such as GitHub, GitLab and Quarto then show an error or an empty placeholder, and the diagram cannot raise either limit itself. The size is counted as mermaid.render() counts it (without the frontmatter and comments, with the newline that ends a code block), and the Mermaid check confirms both limits at the boundary. Hosts that use mermaid.run(), such as pkgdown sites, count up to a few characters less, so the warning there can come a little early, never late. The warning names the options; ?put_diagram and the troubleshooting vignette describe both limits. Large diagrams are also much faster to generate: a 500-step chain took about two minutes, because every input looked through every step’s outputs, and now takes about two seconds. (#56)
  • Consolidated language detection list into single authoritative registry (.LANGUAGES_WITH_DETECTION in language_registry.R)
  • Standardized output parameter across put_diagram(), put_generate(), and putior_guide() – all now support “raw”
  • Extracted duplicated label resolution into resolve_label() helper
  • Added input path sanitization to ACP server endpoints

Backward Compatibility

  • All new parameters default to FALSE/previous behavior
  • Existing code continues to work unchanged
  • putior_workflow class inherits from data.frame, preserving compatibility

putior 0.1.0

CRAN release: 2025-06-19

  • Initial CRAN submission
  • Added put() function for extracting workflow annotations from source code files
  • Added put_diagram() function for creating Mermaid flowchart diagrams
  • Added is_valid_put_annotation() for validating annotation syntax
  • Support for multiple programming languages: R, Python, SQL, Shell, and Julia
  • Multiline annotation support with backslash continuation syntax for better code style compliance
  • Automatic UUID generation when id field is omitted from annotations
  • Automatic output defaulting to file name when output field is omitted
  • Renamed annotation field from name to id for better graph theory alignment
  • Five built-in themes for diagrams: light, dark, auto, minimal, and github
  • Automatic file flow tracking between workflow steps
  • Comprehensive vignette with examples
  • Full test coverage for all major functions
